Currently, some of the world's biggest companies are racing to build strong AGI – best considered Autonomous General Intelligence – which would quickly lead to superintelligence. And with several Apollo projects' worth of spend and effort, they are succeeding.

1898023053864632480 [2025-03-07] @AnthonyNAguirre 💜 4
Almost everyone wants trustworthy and effective AI tools to help in scientific and medical discovery, economic productivity, and general human empowerment.  Tools are great, and tools (of varying quality) are mostly what AI companies have given us so far.
↓
1898023055286583471 [2025-03-07] @AnthonyNAguirre 💜 5
But that's not what's now happening. They're trying, with a complex mix of motivations, to build autonomous machines that can match the full range of human expertise at approximately every intellectual task and job.  Including, explicitly, making stronger AI systems. They are trying to build "a country of a million geniuses in a data center."
↓
1898023056653926465 [2025-03-07] @AnthonyNAguirre 💜 4
How does one control a country of a million geniuses that can think many times faster than humans, copy and extend themselves, and create and enact sophisticated plans toward goals of their own?  The answer is that one doesn't.  That's not a tool, it's a replacement for us, first individually in our jobs, then in actually running our institutions, and eventually as stewards of Earth. On the way it would almost inevitably disrupt and undermine our civilization, and maybe start WWIII to boot.
↓
1898023058029658227 [2025-03-07] @AnthonyNAguirre 💜 4 [(SEED) type=semantic_search]
I wrote Keep the Future Human to give a comprehensive view of the bind humanity has put itself into, and how we can get out. We absolutely can abandon the trajectory toward artificial superintelligence, and instead commit to the great AI tools we actually want instead.  But we'll have to act decisively, and pretty much right now.
↓

Some context about the Future of Life Institute:

FLI is "a non-profit that works to reduce existential risk from powerful technologies, particularly artificial intelligence" (source: Effective Altruism Forum).

In practice, its leaders, mainly Max Tegmark and Jaan Tallinn, have publicly warned of human extinction from AI and advocated for stringent AI regulation. For example, on current models with a compute threshold of 10^25 FLOPs.

According to Tegmark, the threat is imminent: "The artificial intelligence that we're trying to build will probably annihilate all of humanity pretty soon."

Tallinn proposed "banning training runs" and that the surveillance of software and hardware "has to be more and more pervasive."
